To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) CCl(4)-induced liver fibrosis in rats is reversible, (2) silymarin and silibinin are ineffective in the reversal of liver fibrosis and (3) colchicine and TMCA are ineffective in the prevention of liver fibrosis

the discontinuation of CCl4 treatment in the rat for two months, after three months of administration, produced a significant, but relative small reduction in fibrosis (collagens still increased 4.5 fold).

the best scheme of treatment to study the ability to reverse fibrosis is obtained when CCl4 is administered during 3 months, followed by discontinuation of treatment for 2 months, and that colchicine, trimethylcolchinin, silymarine and silibinin show no significant fibrolithic effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of silybin and colchicine on liver fibrosis in rats.
the development of an experimental fibrosis model and with the search for a suitable therapy to reverse it.
the development of an experimental model of liver fibrosis that is reversible and the study of drugs that are able to reverse it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
silymarin and its main constituent, silibinin have no significant effect in reversing liver fibrosis.
the hepatoprotective drugs studied in this work do not reverse established cirrhogenesis.
the model of liver cirrhosis induced by CCl4 is a suitable one to test the ability of drugs, such as colchicine or trimethylcolchicine, to reverse established cirrosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best scheme of treatment to study the ability to reverse fibrosis is to induce fibrosis for 3 months and to discontinue CCl(4).
the best scheme of treatment is to administer CCl(4), 0.4 g/rat three times per week for three months, followed by discontinuation of toxin for two months.
silymarin and silibinin are hepatoprotective drugs, while colchicine and its derivatives are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain a model of cirrhosis in which fibrosis is reversible, but it is difficult to obtain a model in which fibrosis can be completely reversed.
the fibrotic process in the rat liver induced by CCl4 is reversible, at least in part, after discontinuation of the toxic agent.
the fibrotic response of the liver is reversible, at least in the rat, and that the fibrotrophic effect of CCl( 4) is maximal after three months of administration.
